correctness.rationale: The maximal Steiner inellipse is an affine image of the equilateral incircle; its squared semiaxes are proportional to centered-vertex covariance eigenvalues. The exact trace/determinant identity gives K=2R/(1+R^2)=sqrt(3)*product(chords)/sum(squared chords). Isolated equilateral angular coordinates yield a positive-definite quadratic form of determinant 3/4; two normalized ellipsoidal volumes give 3sqrt(3)/(16pi). A global shortest-chord inequality localizes every flat event to pair collisions. A uniform pair-gap derivative sqrt(3)/4 and an O(eta rho) bound on near-triple overlaps give 4sqrt(3)/pi. Converting R=sqrt(1-e^2) gives 4sqrt(6)/pi. Uniform-angle densities on convergent bounded coordinate domains imply the claimed total-variation marked limits. 1000 direct covariance comparisons and Sobol diagnostics passed; numerical checks do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The maximum-area inscribed ellipse of a triangle is a canonical object and its Euclidean axis ratio measures isotropy of that optimally packed convex figure. Exact quartic near-circle rarity versus square-root near-segment rarity, with independently specified marked geometric limits, reveal a clean dichotomy between isolated equilateral configurations and colliding pairs. The coefficients are scale-free and have nontrivial geometric Jacobians; the result is not an arbitrary table entry, a naming convention or a known deterministic ellipse formula.
